acceptance_predicate.claim: For the selected mainnet certificate-v3 block, hash_b equals the keyed BLAKE3 root of a runtime weight slab reconstructed from a frozen public checkpoint revision through the frozen pinned transformation recipe, without miner-provided operand bytes.

contract.rule: Parse the certificate envelope version-first; dispatch strictly on version 3; never parse a V3 body with V1 fixed-size logic even though a dense body is also 164 bytes.
V3 body layout is the V2 layout; ProofCommitment domain is version 3; Salted seed derivation is a property of the version and is not on the wire.

Dense public_data length is exactly 164; any other length for a mainnet V3 certificate at height >= 91630 is consensus-invalid at the pin and must be classified INVALID for reconstruction, not parsed as MoE.

Full block header serialization and the 76-byte IncompleteBlockHeader must be reconstructed from retained header bytes: version LE32 | prev_block (32, wire/internal order) | merkle_root (32, wire/internal order) | timestamp LE32 | nbits LE32. The Go FFI reverses to display order and Rust reverses back; the net preimage uses wire order. Both implementations must document which order they use and produce the identical 76 bytes.
Certificate block-hash binding: certificate.Hash must equal header.BlockHash(); header.ProofCommitment must equal SHA256d(LE32(3) || public_data). Both are checked before any hash_b use.

MiningConfiguration 52 bytes: common_dim LE32 | rank LE16 | mma_type LE16 (0 only) | rows_pattern 6 | cols_pattern 6 | trailer 32 = e LE16 | top_k LE16 | 28 zero bytes; e must be 0 for dense; reserved bytes must be zero; round-trip must be byte-identical.
job_key = BLAKE3(unkeyed)(header_76 || mining_config_52); exactly 128 bytes of preimage.
hash_b is public_data[84:116]; hash_a is [52:84]; hash_jackpot is [116:148]; m,n,t_rows,t_cols are LE32 at [148:164].
int8 values are serialized as two's-complement single bytes; the miner path casts int8 to uint8 modulo 256 before hashing. A saturating or erroring cast is a wrong implementation.
Orientation: the hashed tensor is B_T with shape n x k, row-major, C-contiguous, exactly as passed to the kernel (w_q.contiguous()). A transposed, Fortran-ordered, or strided view is wrong.

Fusion: where the pinned vLLM 0.20.2 path stores fused QKV or fused gate/up parameters, the slab is the fused runtime parameter in runtime order. The exact fused ordering, per-partition sizes, and whether hashing happens per fused parameter or per sub-projection must be frozen from pinned source with file:line before Phase 4. Unresolved -> BLOCKED.

Tensor parallelism: the TP degree set and the row/column slicing rule per parameter class must be frozen from pinned vLLM source with file:line. Every TP rank of every enumerated degree is a distinct registry slab. Unresolved -> BLOCKED.

Expert parallelism, MoE stacking, per-expert n versus stacked rows: out of scope by consensus exclusion; any MoE artifact in the V3 lane is INVALID. Registry may contain MoE models only if their dense (non-expert) parameters are enumerated as dense slabs under the frozen recipe.
Padding: zero-pad to a multiple of 1024 bytes; leaf count = ceil(len/1024); root = standard keyed BLAKE3 of the padded bytes. Unpadded, doubly padded, or leaf-size-mismatched constructions are wrong.

Every transform parameter in the recipe has status fixed with source, or the run is BLOCKED before Phase 4. No default may be inferred from convenience, from a matching shape, or from the observed target.

Material not bound by hash_b and therefore outside any E-000 claim: weight scales, SmoothQuant scales, Hadamard block size, layer identity, model identity, checkpoint revision, tokenizer, request, activations, output. A MATCH identifies a slab byte-string, not a model execution.

byte_path_requirements.target_function: hash_b == BLAKE3_keyed(key=job_key, data=zero_pad_to_1024(row_major_int8_bytes(B_T))) where B_T is the runtime weight slab as passed to the mining kernel (shape n x k)

candidate_selection_rule.blinding_statement: Genuine cryptographic blinding is unavailable: hash_b is public. The strongest auditable separation is temporal: the candidate must not exist when the registry, recipe, and implementation are frozen and operator-accepted. Same-machine procedural separation is auditable ordering, not concealment.
forbidden: choosing T_accept after any candidate data is observed
re-running selection with a different T_start or window
selecting by shape, model, or any public_data content beyond PublicDataLen
inserting a height, hash, certificate, hash_b, or checkpoint identity into this freeze
inputs: T_accept: UTC time of the operator acceptance record that cites this file's SHA-256
public mainnet header metadata after T_accept
candidate_selection_rule.selection_time_bias_note: The candidate is a block that did not exist at acceptance. Neither owner nor reviewer can have pre-computed its hash_b classification. Miner-side bias is out of scope for E-000 and irrelevant to the reconstruction question.
steps: S1. Let T_start = T_accept + 3600 s. This margin exceeds MaxTimeOffsetMinutes (5 min) and several mainnet target intervals (3 min 14 s).
S2. Let H_ref be the lowest mainnet height whose header timestamp >= T_start, as agreed by two independent public sources.
S3. Scan heights h = H_ref, H_ref+1, ... in ascending order. The candidate is the first h satisfying all eligibility predicates.

S4. Eligibility predicates: (a) network is mainnet per pinned params; (b) h >= 99000; (c) certificate version field == 3; (d) PublicDataLen == 164; (e) confirmation depth >= 100 at both sources at retrieval time; (f) block hash identical at both sources; (g) consensus-drift check passes (no consensus rule activated between the pinned commit and height h in the public Pearl repository that alters certificate envelope, public_data layout, job_key derivation, mining_config encoding, or hash_b construction).
S5. Tie-breaking: none needed; heights are totally ordered and the first eligible height is unique.

S6. Exhaustion: if no eligible height exists among the first 2000 heights at or above H_ref, or the chain has not reached H_ref+100 confirmations within 14 days of T_accept, terminal state is BLOCKED with code E000-BLK-NO-ELIGIBLE-CANDIDATE. No later window may be chosen for this experiment ID.
S7. A V3 certificate at h >= 99000 with PublicDataLen != 164 is consensus-invalid at the pin and is recorded as E000-INV-CONSENSUS-CONTRADICTION; the scan continues, and the anomaly must be reported.

S8. Non-self-mined: the operator records a signed attestation that no Pearl mining was ever performed from any operator-controlled key, machine, or pool account, and the candidate's coinbase outputs are retained. This is attestation, not proof; public data cannot exclude self-mining.

evidence_requirements.no_weights_in_repo: No model weight file or any fragment of one may be committed to Aeye. Only digests, shapes, names, and retrieval receipts are retained.

evidence_requirements.registry_freeze_rule: After Phase 3 no model, revision, tensor, TP/EP layout, or transformation may be added, removed, or edited for this experiment ID. The registry digest is content-addressed and cited by the run manifest.
evidence_requirements.temporal_provenance_rule: Phase 3 (registry freeze) completes before Phase 4 (selection), and the candidate is a future block. Therefore every registry revision predates the candidate by Aeye's own retrieval receipt time, independent of publisher-asserted timestamps. Publisher timestamps are recorded but never load-bearing.
evidence_requirements.timestamp_insufficiency: A checkpoint 'last updated' timestamp alone is insufficient. Immutable git revision history and exact file digests are required; if unavailable for a repo, that repo is OUT of the registry.

trust_tiers.T1: T0 + pinned git revision SHA + retrieval receipts + per-file sha256 + second retrieval over an independent network path
trust_tiers.T2: T1 + independent reproduction of the quantized checkpoint from a different publisher's base model and published recipe

implementation_independence_requirements.definition: Two implementations are independent for E-000 when they share no Aeye-authored source file, module, function, or fixture generator for envelope parsing, header/config serialization, job_key derivation, checkpoint parsing, transformation, padding, hashing orchestration, or comparison; when they were written against the pinned Pearl source rather than against each other; and when at least one differs from the other in programming language or in tensor-file parsing library.
explicit_non_claims: code-path separation is not peer review
implementation_independence_requirements.pearl_parity_oracle: The pinned pearl-blake3 MerkleTree and the pinned Python MatrixMerkleTree (or its documented CPU equivalent) must reproduce the root on the frozen slab bytes and on every known-bad fixture. Reusing Pearl code inside either Aeye implementation is not independence; Pearl code is oracle only.
permitted_shared_primitives: a BLAKE3 implementation, provided both pass the official BLAKE3 keyed-mode test vectors and at least one of the two is not the same codebase as the other (for example upstream library versus an independent reference implementation)
the checkpoint bytes themselves and their frozen digests
the pinned Pearl checkout as read-only oracle
residual_common_mode_risks: both authors are the same implementation owner and may share a misreading of the vLLM transform
both may read the same misdocumented pinned source line
both may share an upstream BLAKE3 keyed-mode bug
both run on one workstation and one operating system
implementation_independence_requirements.third_party_replay: A single documented command, taking only retained public artifacts and the frozen registry identities, must reproduce every transcript stage and the terminal classification without network access other than optional re-download of checkpoint files verified against frozen digests.
implementation_independence_requirements.transcript_comparison: Byte-for-byte equality is required at every stage: header_76, mining_config_52, job_key, per-source-tensor digests, fused/sliced slab bytes digest and shape, padded length and leaf count, root. Equal final roots with a divergent intermediate is a FAIL of the run (E000-INV-TRANSCRIPT-DIVERGENCE), not a pass.

independence_limit.statement: This freeze is same-workstation machine adversarial review. It establishes auditable ordering and pre-outcome criteria only. It does not establish organizational, institutional, cryptographic, hardware, custody, or human independence, and it is not peer review.

definitions.BLOCKED: Before Phase 8 a prerequisite could not be met: unresolved transform parameter, registry not freezable at T1, no eligible candidate within the exhaustion rule, consensus drift, oracle parity failure, or security stop. Not a scientific negative.
definitions.INVALID: A protocol violation occurred: phase order broken, prohibited observation, edit after reveal, digest mismatch, transcript divergence, version-route mismatch discovered after Phase 4, consensus contradiction in the candidate, or discovery after reveal that a recipe parameter was unresolved. No scientific classification is emitted; the violation code is retained.
definitions.IN_COVERAGE_NO_MATCH: Shape is in the index, every registry slab of that shape across all frozen models, revisions, TP degrees, and transforms was computed by both implementations with agreement, and none equals hash_b. Permitted phrasing: 'did not open to any registered slab'. Never 'random', 'non-model', or 'FALSE'.
definitions.MATCH: At least one frozen registry slab's root equals hash_b byte-for-byte, with both implementations and the Pearl oracle agreeing at every transcript stage. Report the set of matching slab ids; identical slabs across revisions are one byte-string.
definitions.OUT_OF_COVERAGE: The candidate's (n, k) from public_data has no slab in the frozen registry shape index. Evidence of nothing about the miner.
definitions.UNRETRIEVED: An eligible candidate exists but its header or certificate bytes could not be retrieved consistently from two independent public sources under the retrieval policy. Reported; never dropped.

terminal_states.fb4a_relationship: MATCH discharges FB-4a (recomputability) for this candidate and registry only. IN_COVERAGE_NO_MATCH or OUT_OF_COVERAGE does not falsify FB-4a for the network; it falsifies public reconstruction only for this candidate against this registry and recipe.
never: render missing, unsupported, unmeasured, or unavailable as zero or success
call absence of a match FALSE
compute a rate from a single opening
terminal_states.single_opening_legality: IN_COVERAGE_NO_MATCH is legal for the single-opening experiment only because Phase 7 requires exhaustive enumeration of every registry slab of the candidate's shape before reveal. If enumeration is discovered incomplete after reveal, the state is INVALID, never IN_COVERAGE_NO_MATCH.

facts.fact: MsgCertificate is version-first; version 3 decodes to CertificateV3
CertificateV3 embeds CertificateV2 and overrides only Version and ProofCommitment (hashes version 3)
CertificateV2 layout: BlockHash(32) | PublicDataLen(4 LE) | PublicData | ProofLen(4 LE) | ProofData; PublicDataMaxSizeV2=4807; dense size 164; IsMoE() := PublicDataLen > 164
Node dispatch: CertificateV3 -> verifyCertificateV3 -> FFI verify_zk_proof_v3; CertificateV1 -> verify_zk_proof_v1
SeedDerivation is selected by certificate version, never serialized, no Default; Salted salts roots before the unchanged seed chain; wire carries raw roots
zk-pow/src/v1 is the V1 (master) verifier compatibility path
V2/V3 from_wire_bytes rejects a 164-byte body whose mining_config selects GROUPED_GEMM and rejects a MoE tail whose mining_config is dense
Mainnet consensus at pin: RequiredCertVersion(height) is V3 for height >= 99000; MoE certificates rejected for height >= 91630
V1 MiningConfiguration trailer is 32 reserved bytes; V2/V3 trailer is e(2)|top_k(2)|28 zero bytes with e==0 meaning dense. Dense bytes coincide; semantics differ

pab_note_correction_required.defect: Claims certificate-v3 scope but cites zk-pow/src/v1/api and zk-pow/src/v1/circuit paths and a fixed 164-byte public data; V3 verification executes zk-pow/src/api and zk-pow/src/circuit and admits variable-length MoE public data in the parser.
pab_note_correction_required.required_correction: Re-cite every fact from zk-pow/src/api, zk-pow/src/circuit, and zk-pow/src/ffi at the pinned commit; state that Salted derivation applies; state that 164 bytes is the dense-only length; add the MoE variable-length case or state the dense-only consensus exclusion with its height gate. Reviewer does not edit the note.

verified_version_route.summary: CertificateV3 shares the CertificateV2 variable-length envelope and routes through zk-pow/src/api with SeedDerivation::Salted. zk-pow/src/v1 is the legacy CertificateV1 verifier and is never executed for a V3 certificate. Salting alters the noise-seed chain, not hash_b.
